title: In Matthew 23 How Can We Ensure That We Prioritize The Weightier Matters Of The Law In Our Own Faith Practices
paragraphs: Understanding the “Weightier Matters” in Matthew 23

Matthew 23 is a chapter filled with Jesus’ strong words to the religious leaders of His day. In this passage, Jesus addresses the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, warning them—and us—not to neglect the most important aspects of God’s law while becoming overly focused on minor details.
The Key Passage: Matthew 23:23

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye tithe mint and anise and cummin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law, justice, and mercy, and faith: but these ye ought to have done, and not to have left the other undone. -
Matthew 23:23 ASV

Here, Jesus affirms the value of detailed obedience (“these ye ought to have done”) but rebukes the leaders for missing what He calls the “weightier matters” of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. Jesus is not dismissing external obedience but insisting that true righteousness prioritizes the heart and character of God’s law.
Exploring the Weightier Matters

Justice: God cares deeply about fairness and righteousness in our relationships. Throughout Scripture, God commands His people to act justly (Micah 6:8 ASV), to defend the oppressed, and to stand against injustice.

Mercy: Mercy reflects God’s own compassionate heart. Jesus repeatedly taught the importance of mercy over ritual sacrifice (Matthew 9:13 ASV). True faith is demonstrated in tangible acts of kindness and forgiveness.
Faith: Biblical faith is more than mere belief; it is trust and fidelity to God. Hebrews reminds us, “And without faith it is impossible to be well-pleasing unto him...” (Hebrews 11:6 ASV).
Why Do We Miss the Weightier Matters?

Like the Pharisees, we can be tempted to focus on visible, measurable actions—church attendance, giving, or external behaviors—while overlooking the deeper issues of the heart. Jesus’ critique warns us against a checklist faith that neglects transformation and love.
But the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter; but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness. -
Luke 11:39 ASV
How Can We Prioritize the Weightier Matters Today?
Examine Our Hearts Regularly: Ask God to reveal areas where we may be focusing on minor issues while neglecting love, justice, or faithfulness (Psalm 139:23 ASV).
Practice Justice, Mercy, and Faith: Look for practical ways to demonstrate fairness, show compassion, and live out our trust in Christ each day, in our homes, workplaces, and communities.

Keep Christ Central: Remember that Jesus Himself is the fulfillment of the law and embodies its weightiest matters. We follow Him not by mere external conformity but by being transformed by His Spirit (Romans 8:4 ASV).
Balance Both Sides: Jesus doesn’t say to neglect the details (“not to have left the other undone”), but to ensure our obedience flows from a heart aligned with God’s priorities.
The Gospel Motivation

The call to justice, mercy, and faith is not a burden but a reflection of the grace we have received in Christ. We love and serve because He first loved us (1 John 4:19 ASV). Our salvation is by grace through faith, not by works (Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV), but true saving faith always produces the fruit of godly character.
Conclusion

Prioritizing the weightier matters of the law means letting God’s love shape every part of our lives. As we trust in Christ and yield to His Spirit, He empowers us to live out justice, mercy, and faith in a world that desperately needs to see His character through us.
